solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charm one's way in?

definitions.meaning: a door or gateway through which you go in

explanation.surface: Could a smooth talker simply charm their way through the door?
explanation.definitionFit: The verb (stress on the second syllable) means to enchant; the noun (stress on the first) is a doorway, two unrelated senses spelt alike.

clue.text: Take advantage of exit poll almost being wrong

indicators.note: being wrong says these letters are set out incorrectly, in a new order
almost means the phrase stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an exit poll surveys voters as they leave the polling station

explanation.surface: A pundit seizes on a nearly inaccurate exit poll to score a political point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims EXITPOLL to EXITPOL, and 'being wrong' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it for your own benefit, often unfairly.

clue.text: Stomach for eating rubbish

definitions.meaning: the stomach lining of a cow or sheep, cooked as food
informal for nonsense or worthless stuff

explanation.surface: Someone with no appetite for eating junk food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is both an offal dish made from stomach lining and slang for nonsense.

clue.text: Atmospheric flow pattern, neatly conic in circulation

indicators.note: in circulation suggests letters spinning round into a new order, fitting the weather surface

explanation.surface: A weather report describing air flowing neatly round in a cone shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticyclone is a high-pressure weather system whose winds circulate outward around its centre.

clue.text: Conservative supporter keeping millions coolly

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an ally is someone who backs you
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A Tory backer coolly hanging on to vast sums of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts M inside CALLY, after CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To act coolly is to act without agitation, in a composed, unruffled way.

clue.text: Change over hands, right to left

indicators.note: right to left means the word is read in the opposite direction from normal

parts.note: paws is informal for hands

explanation.surface: Switching an object from one hand to the other, right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, an idiomatic match for changing over.

clue.text: Swimmer dealt a blow in flank

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other here

parts.note: a wing is the flank or side of an army or team
to hit is to deal a blow

explanation.surface: A sea creature struck on its side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flank' is a noun here, the side of an army, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The whiting is a sea fish; crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: King perhaps wants an end to hostilities declared

indicators.note: declared means spoken out loud, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: peace is the end of fighting

explanation.surface: A monarch seeking to have a truce proclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declared' signals a sound-alike: PEACE is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The king is one of the chessmen in a chess set; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Spot beer, getting round in

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a pint is a standard measure of beer in a British pub
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Noticing a pal's beer as they buy a round at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is O, not a round of drinks; 'in' puts it inside PINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A point is a dot or small mark, so it means spot as a noun.

clue.text: Like older buildings with fancy oriels round either side of window

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the single letter
fancy suggests letters arranged decoratively, a new order
either side of means one of the outer letters, which are both the same here

explanation.surface: Old houses with ornate bay windows set on both sides of a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges ORIELS to LORISE; 'either side of' gives W, as WINDOW starts and ends with it; 'round' puts LORISE around it. An oriel is a projecting upper-floor window.
explanation.definitionFit: Older buildings tend to have few storeys, which is what low-rise describes.

clue.text: Several new among reds, say, with sulphur and appealing quality

indicators.note: among puts these letters within the other word

parts.note: red wines are an example of wines
some means several
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A wine buff noting some new reds with sulphites have charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reds, say' points to wines in general, with 'say' marking reds as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsomeness is charm or engaging attractiveness, a quality that appeals.

clue.text: Joined English National Opera on retirement

indicators.note: on retirement means going backwards, withdrawing, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ENO is the abbreviation for English National Opera

explanation.surface: A singer who joined the opera company just as it was winding down.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined together have become one, a single united whole, as in 'at one'.

clue.text: Wild growth in free line dance

indicators.note: free suggests letters let loose to land in a new order

explanation.surface: A spontaneous line dance growing wild and unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: The celandine is a small yellow wild flower, so it is a plant growing wild.

clue.text: Material for roofing the little church over there?

parts.note: pointing at something distant, you might say 'that' one
CH is the short form of church

explanation.surface: Asking whether the quaint chapel in the distance has a straw roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the little church over there' reads as 'that church', shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reed laid as a covering on a roof.

clue.text: One feeling for insect in a number trapped by girl

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside, so the number goes within the name

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A girl trapping a few insects in a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One feeling' is a feeler, not an emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's antenna is a sensory feeler, used to feel its way about.

clue.text: Big cat is company, a sweet thing — but not small

indicators.note: but not small says the letter for small is dropped

parts.note: sugar is a sweet substance

explanation.surface: A puma's company is a pleasant thing, though hardly a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not small' removes S (small) from SUGAR, leaving UGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar, or puma, is a large wild feline of the Americas.

clue.text: Not all red lentils, say, cause aversion

indicators.note: not all of the word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
lentils are an example of a pulse, an edible seed

explanation.surface: Some red lentils and the like put diners off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' trims RED to RE; 'Not all' looks like it signals a hidden word in 'red lentils', but it does not.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse is to disgust or repel, causing a feeling of revulsion.

clue.text: Joshing in bar, they're regularly ignored

parts.note: to ban is to bar or prohibit

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is skipped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: Pub jokes in a bar where the regulars get ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops alternate letters of THEYRE, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Banter is playful teasing talk, the same as joking or joshing.

clue.text: Support pageant or plays

indicators.note: plays suggests letters moving about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Backing theatre, whether a pageant or plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronage is the backing or sponsorship a patron gives to the arts.

clue.text: American nut exercises about noon

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
CA (circa) means about

explanation.surface: An American nut doing a workout around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a nut from a hickory tree native to North America.

clue.text: Fizzy drink for father

explanation.surface: A soft drink bought for dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop names both a sparkling soft drink and, informally, a dad.

clue.text: Copier under pressure in exam

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts this piece below the other

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
an aper is one who apes, copying others

explanation.surface: A cheat copying answers under the stress of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places APER beneath P in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam paper is the set of questions a candidate sits, so paper stands for the exam itself.

clue.text: Study printed work and background

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
a text is a printed book or work

explanation.surface: Studying a printed book along with its background.
explanation.definitionFit: The context of something is its surrounding circumstances, the setting that explains it.

clue.text: Half expected learner to drive out

indicators.note: half means only the first four of these eight letters are used

parts.note: L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A learner driver half expected to set off.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force out or eject someone.

clue.text: What may be seen in one area close by

indicators.note: what may be seen in means the letters sit visibly inside these words

explanation.surface: Something visible nearby in a single district.
explanation.definitionFit: Near means at a short distance away, nearby.

clue.text: Keep quiet with book

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: A librarian asking for silence while holding onto a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to maintain it or save it from harm.
